content:
Looks pretty interesting. ChatGPT's latest update has added a new Mac integration feature: the ability to handle conversations in Apple's Messages app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now has an Apple Messages plugin

The new Apple Messages plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search chat histories on Mac, as well as prepare and send messages. OpenAI says this feature is available across all plans on the ChatGPT macOS desktop app, and is supported by both ChatGPT and Codex.

Because of the access permissions involved, naturally raising concerns about privacy and control, OpenAI emphasises that, under default settings, sending messages must receive user approval. Users should carefully consider before granting persistent approval permissions. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the related risks, how to revoke permissions, and a known issue involving bypassing approval prompts.

For now, this feature is only available on Macs equipped with Apple silicon; Intel machines miss out.

If you ask ChatGPT to send a message on your behalf, the system will pop up a confirmation prompt before sending. You can also choose to skip this confirmation step within individual conversations.

Want to find this new feature in ChatGPT? The link below will take you directly to the Messages plugin for Mac ChatGPT.

Site co-editing, shared thread snapshots, and more

Although the Messages plugin is the headline new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now stay synced between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, allowing users to access important conversations anytime between Mac and iPhone.

ChatGPT now also lets users share read-only snapshots of local Codex threads. These snapshots will not change when the original thread is updated.

Links generated from personal accounts can be opened by anyone who has the URL; workspace links, however, are restricted to members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex will mask known sensitive formats, but reminds users to check their own snapshots, as they may still contain sensitive data.

Additionally, Site owners can invite existing members of the same workspace to co-edit Sites with the collaboration feature enabled. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish updates after the owner completes the initial publish. Owners still retain control over access, settings, analytics, and version restoration.

Some Site owners can also change ChatGPT-hosted URLs without redeploying, with old addresses automatically redirecting to the new address.

Finally, the Computer Use History feature launched last week is expanding to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This opt-in feature requires the Memory feature to be enabled, and is off by default.

You can see the full release notes for this update here.
